story:
You are there in Bethlehem, huddled in the warmth of a stable tucked against a hillside. The air is cool and smells of hay and animals—so different from the crowded streets outside. You can feel the soft straw beneath you as you peer into the manger, where something miraculous has just happened.

A baby lies sleeping, wrapped in strips of cloth, his tiny face peaceful and perfect. This is Jesus, born on this quiet night while the world outside sleeps. His mother, Mary, watches him with wonder in her eyes, so tenderly, as if she still can't believe this precious child is hers. Joseph stands nearby, strong and gentle, protecting them both.

The shepherds who brought you here are still amazed. Just hours ago, they were in the fields with their sheep when the sky suddenly blazed with light brighter than a thousand stars. An angel appeared—so bright and so full of joy—telling them that the Savior had been born, right here in this little town. And they came running, their hearts full of excitement and awe.

Now, in this quiet moment, you feel it too—something holy and tender filling the stable. The baby's chest rises and falls gently. Mary hums a soft lullaby. And you understand: God's great love has come to earth in the form of this sleeping child.

Outside, the night is still and peaceful. Everything is calm. Everything is safe. And you drift toward sleep with the warmth of knowing you are loved beyond measure.
title: The Night Jesus Was Born
verseText: "She gave birth to her firstborn son and wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn." — Luke 2:7
moral: God's greatest gift to the world was born in gentleness and love, and that same love watches over you every night.
